glosses: vanity

examples.text: Со вре́мени сближе́ния при́нца с его́ жено́ю, Пьер неожи́данно был пожа́лован в камерге́ры, и с э́того вре́мени он стал чу́вствовать тя́жесть и стыд в большо́м о́бществе, и ча́ще ему́ ста́ли приходи́ть пре́жние мра́чные мы́сли о тщете́ всего́ челове́ческого.
examples.translation: Since the intimacy of his wife with the royal prince, Pierre had unexpectedly been made a gentleman of the bedchamber, and from that time he had begun to feel oppressed and ashamed in court society, and dark thoughts of the vanity of all things human came to him oftener than before.
examples.english: Since the intimacy of his wife with the royal prince, Pierre had unexpectedly been made a gentleman of the bedchamber, and from that time he had begun to feel oppressed and ashamed in court society, and dark thoughts of the vanity of all things human came to him oftener than before.

glosses: That which is vain, futile, or worthless; that which is of no value, use or profit.

examples.text: Then I said in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me and why then was I more wise? Then I said in my heart that this is also vanity. / For there is no more remembrance of the wise than the fool forever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.

glosses: Excessive pride in or admiration of one's own abilities, appearance, achievements, or possessions.

examples.text: To make a man in love with you gives an instant hold on his vanity; and with that, you can do any thing. Vanity is the real lever with which Archimedes said he could move the earth; so, try what you can effect with Sir Robert.
